did: Clicked the Admiralty link 'Dumonceau, march to Normandy' (6,500 men, 4 provinces to the yard)
expected: the link to say what it costs before I pressed it, or to ask first
saw: it executed at once and spent 2 of my 4 actions (a standing march); the link text names men and provinces but not the 2 AP price, and I only learned of it from the 2/4 counter

did: Napoleon was marching to Flanders (1 turn left). A 'Cannon fire at Franche-Comte, Sire. Investigate?' pop-up came with three buttons; I pressed 'Continue as Ordered'
expected: Napoleon would carry on to Flanders and arrive next turn, as I had ordered
saw: the morning dispatch says Napoleon is HALTED at Orleanais - awaiting your word (Soult, with the same order, arrived). So 'Continue as Ordered' stopped my march and cost me a turn of the camp; nothing told me it would

did: The morning dispatch said of Massena 'Morale failing (0) - two turns of drill would steady them'; I typed 'Massena, drill'
saw: 'Massena is recovering from retreat and cannot drill. Recovery: 2 turns remaining.' The dispatch advice and the refusal contradict each other; nothing in the dispatch said drill is closed during recovery

did: Murat's audience card offered 'Give him a command (2 AP) - Send him against Mack into Munich'. I took it (earlier this turn Ney had beaten Mack at Munich)
expected: Murat to attack Mack at Munich as the card said, or the card to say Mack was gone
saw: Mack had already retreated to Tyrol, so Murat was sent to 'pursue Archduke Charles' at Franconia instead - I never chose that - and he lost 5,379 men to Charles's 2,632, alone ('Ney never came'). 2 AP spent and a corps bled on a target the card did not name

did: Clicked 'Land Dumonceau here' on Ulster to raise Ireland; read the 'Dumonceau asks' quote before sailing
expected: to be told what a successful landing does - what Dumonceau would do in Ulster, whether it raises Ireland, what he fights
saw: the quote lists only the odds (72 in 100), the failure costs (30% lost, a decisive defeat halving every pooled fleet) and what moves the odds; nothing about the prize. The region panel says only 'Stripped? unknown - scout it'. I must gamble half the fleet without knowing what winning gets me

did: Accepted Austria's 'Armistice' (5-turn ceasefire, marked GENEROUS). Its terms said Bavaria stays at war and '5 French corps stand on Bavarian soil under the truce'
expected: my five corps on Bavarian soil to stay where they were, or at least to be asked
saw: next turn the log says Ney, Davout, Lannes, Murat and Bernadotte were each 'put on the road home ... to Nivernais under the truce - 5 turns' (my corps marched out of Bavaria on their own, and Ney's 2-AP march to Swabia of the turn before was wasted); Bavaria was then 'Eliminated' by Austria. The terms never said the truce would march my armies home or that my ally would be left alone

did: Told Soult (30,000, the main body of the invasion camp at Flanders) to 'pursue Paget' (1 AP). Two turns earlier the Admiralty had said the camp had lifted Britain's blockade
expected: a word that moving him out of the camp province breaks the camp and brings the blockade back
saw: 'Soult pursues Paget. Moves to Orleanais.' and nothing else. The next income line shows 'Blockade: -320g' again - the camp count reset and the blockade is back. The Admiralty page says a march out resets the count, but the order that does it never says so

did: At the Britain-alone table with 'Erect Ireland' demanded (Britain 17/50), pressed 'More generous' until it stopped at 1,000g and 26/50, then 'Ease Britain' and 'More generous' again
expected: either more of my 5,241 spare gold to be offered, or a line saying the generosity limit was reached and what else could move Britain
saw: both buttons silently do nothing (the panel is 'unchanged'); the table still says 'Use More generous until each accepts' while the button no longer works; the gold line has [-][+] but I could not make [+] respond; I cannot tell whether 26/50 is a ceiling or a missed control

did: With Archduke Charles one march from Paris, ordered Soult and Napoleon (camp at Flanders) 'march to Paris'
expected: a short road to the capital, or to be told before the order is spent how many turns it takes
saw: 'Route: Westphalia -> Artois -> Paris. Moves to Westphalia.' - the road runs through Westphalia (away from where the map shows Paris), 3 turns, into a province that feeds 15,000 for 37,692 men ('~1,231 a turn lost'). The same came up turn 1 ('Lorraine -> Orleanais -> Flanders') and for Davout (Nivernais -> Burgundy -> Limousin -> Paris, 4 turns). The route and its turn count are only shown after the order is paid for
